sentiment.rationale: Forward guidance was effectively reduced relative to the company's own prior trajectory. Management explicitly stated it was 'not satisfied with our Q4 revenue performance' and that Q4 revenue growth of 14% was below expectations, with the CFO noting 'our largest retail advertisers created a more meaningful headwind than we expected.' Q1 2026 guidance of 11%-14% growth represents a deceleration from the 14% reported in Q4, and management flagged 'year-over-year adjusted EBITDA margin pressure in the first half' of 2026. The cautious, defensive tone regarding near-term headwinds from large retailer pullbacks and the salesforce restructuring, combined with the decelerating growth outlook, warrants a negative score.

summary.revenue: Q4 2025 revenue was $1,319 million, up 14% year-over-year (13% on a constant currency basis). Full year 2025 revenue was $4,222 million, up 16% year-over-year (15% on a constant currency basis).
summary.eps: Q4 2025 GAAP diluted EPS was $0.41, down from $2.68 in Q4 2024. Full year 2025 GAAP diluted EPS was $0.61, down from $2.67 in 2024. Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $0.67 for Q4 2025, up from $0.56 in Q4 2024, and $1.60 for full year 2025, up from $1.29 in 2024.
summary.guidance: For Q1 2026, the company expects revenue in the range of $951 million to $971 million, representing 11%-14% growth year-over-year, with an approximately 3-point tailwind from foreign exchange. Q1 2026 Adjusted EBITDA is expected to be in the range of $166 million to $186 million. The company expects full year 2026 adjusted EBITDA margin to be roughly in line with 2025 at approximately 30%, but approximately 29% including the impact of the TV Scientific acquisition.
summary.margin: Q4 2025 Adjusted EBITDA margin was 41%, up 20 basis points year-over-year. Full year 2025 Adjusted EBITDA margin was 30%. GAAP net income margin for Q4 2025 was 21%.
key_risks: Large retail advertisers pulled back on ad spend due to tariff and margin pressure, creating a more meaningful headwind than expected.
Revenue growth in Europe was below expectations due to pullback by large global retailers.
Ad pricing declined 19% year-over-year due to mix shift towards under-monetized international impressions.
Salesforce and go-to-market restructuring may cause near-term disruption and impact Q1 performance as new hires ramp up.
TV Scientific acquisition is expected to cause a roughly 100 basis point drag to 2026 adjusted EBITDA margin.
Management expects year-over-year adjusted EBITDA margin pressure in the first half of 2026.
Cost of revenue headwinds of approximately 100 basis points in 2026 due to GPU investments for AI initiatives.
key_opportunities: Record user growth with 619 million global MAUs, up 12% year-over-year, marking ten consecutive quarters of record high users.
AI model deployments (OmniSage, PinFM) drove significant engagement gains, with a 450 basis point lift in sitewide saves from OmniSage and a 240 basis point increase from PinFM.
Managed SMB business doubled its year-over-year growth rate in 2025 and now comprises 15% of revenue.
Pinterest Assistant beta launch shows users have 25 percentage points higher commercial intent in queries than with traditional search.
International revenue growth accelerated to 38% in 2025 compared to 25% in 2024.
TV Scientific acquisition supports monetization beyond owned properties and opens up larger, incremental budget pools in connected TV.
Pinterest Performance Plus New Customer Acquisition beta showed a 64% average increase in new customer conversions for test advertisers.

management_tone.label: mixed
management_tone.justification: Management expressed confidence in the long-term opportunity and user engagement ('We're confident these important changes will make us a stronger company and position us to realize the long-term opportunity ahead') but was explicitly cautious and defensive about near-term performance, stating 'we are not satisfied with our Q4 revenue performance' and acknowledging 'near-term disruption' from restructuring.

review_flags.reason: The score of -0.50 reflects a deceleration in forward guidance (Q1 2026 growth of 11-14% vs Q4 2025 growth of 14%) and explicit management caution. However, the company did not formally 'cut' guidance; it provided a new quarter's guidance that is lower than the prior quarter's actual growth. A reviewer should confirm this interpretation of 'guidance reduced' is appropriate versus a more neutral 'in-line' reading.

The GAAP EPS decline is primarily due to a one-time tax benefit in Q4 2024. The non-GAAP EPS shows growth. The summary includes both to provide context, but a reviewer should verify the presentation is clear.
